# Zomato Restaurant, Menu & Review Data Extractor

Turn Zomato's public pages into a clean dataset of restaurants, dishes, reviews and photos for India and the UAE. Paste a city, a listing link, a collection or a restaurant link and the actor returns structured rows you can load into a spreadsheet, database or warehouse. No Zomato account, cookie or proxy setup is needed.

Zomato shows nine restaurants per listing page on the web. This actor does not pretend otherwise: it reads the listings and collections that are actually published, and it exposes the menu, review and photo surfaces that other tools often skip.

## What you can collect

| Mode | Input | One row per |
|---|---|---|
| Search | city + optional cuisine, rating, sort, cost filters, or any listing URL | restaurant |
| Collections | one or more collection URLs, or a city | restaurant |
| Restaurant | restaurant URLs or numeric IDs | restaurant |
| Reviews | restaurant URLs or numeric IDs | review |
| Menu | restaurant URLs or numeric IDs | dish (or a menu-page row when the menu is image-only) |
| Photos | restaurant URLs or numeric IDs | gallery photo |

Every mode accepts numeric restaurant IDs such as `18619718`, so you can start from a CRM or an earlier export without hunting for URLs.

## Restaurant fields

The original fields are all still present, so existing tasks and integrations keep working:

`id`, `res_id`, `name`, `url`, `type`, `cuisines`, `establishments`, `status`, `timing`, `is_delivery_only`, `is_perm_closed`, `location` (`address`, `locality`, `locality_verbose`, `city`, `city_id`, `country`, `country_id`, `zipcode`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `map_url`), `ratings` (`aggregate`, `text`, `votes`, `dining`, `delivery`), `reviews.count`, `price` (`for_two`, `currency`, `currencyCode`, `cft_text`), `phones`, `photo`, `images`, `image_count`, `features`, `highlights`, `known_for`, `top_dishes`, `social.website`, `search_context`.

New fields sit beside them:

- `ratingText`, `ratingSubtitle`, `ratingColor`, `diningReviewCount`, `deliveryReviewCount`
- `timingByDay` (day range + opening hours), `peopleLiked`, `topTags`, `similarRestaurantIds`
- `offers` (title, subtitle, type, value, start and end time), `paymentMethods`, `chain`, `safety`
- `isDarkKitchen`, `is_temp_closed`, `fssai`
- `menuImages` (label, page count), `menuItems` and `menuImagePages` when `includeMenu` is on
- `reviewItems` when `includeReviews` is on, plus `photos` and `photoCount` when `includePhotos` is on

A field Zomato does not publish for a restaurant is omitted, not filled with null or a placeholder.

## Review fields

`reviewId`, `restaurantId`, `restaurantName`, `restaurantUrl`, `city`, `locality`, `text`, `userName`, `userProfileUrl`, `userProfilePic`, `userReviewsCount`, `userFollowersCount`, `rating`, `ratingType`, `experience`, `timestampText`, `reviewDate`, `dateIsApproximate`, `likeCount`, `commentCount`, `comments`, `ownerReplies`, `photos`, `tags`, `reviewUrl`.

`reviewDate` is derived from Zomato's relative label (for example "3 days ago") and is marked approximate; exact dates shown by Zomato are kept as-is.

## Dish fields

`id`, `restaurantId`, `restaurantName`, `restaurantUrl`, `name`, `description`, `price`, `minPrice`, `maxPrice`, `currency`, `currencyCode`, `imageUrl`, `thumbUrl`, `isVeg`, `dietaryTags`, `tags`, `itemType`, `itemState`, `rating`, `ratingVotes`, `menu`, `category`, `modifiers`.

Prices are the amounts Zomato displays to a signed-out visitor. Taxes and charges are not included.

## Photo fields

`photoId`, `restaurantId`, `restaurantName`, `restaurantUrl`, `url`, `thumbUrl`, `uploaderName`, `uploaderProfileUrl`, `timestamp`, `likeCount`, `commentCount`.

## Inputs

| Input | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `search` | Search, Collections, Restaurant, Reviews, Menu or Photos |
| `startUrls` | `[]` | Any Zomato listing, locality, collection, restaurant or share URL, or a numeric restaurant ID |
| `city` | – (prefilled: `mumbai`) | City used by Search and Collections when no listing URL is supplied |
| `searchMode` | `dining` | Dining out, Delivery, Cafes or Drinks & nightlife |
| `cuisine` | Any | Cuisine filter with 120+ options |
| `cuisineSlug` | – | Free-form cuisine ID or slug, overrides the dropdown |
| `minRating` | Any | 3.5+, 4.0+, 4.5+ or 5.0 |
| `sort` | Popularity | Popularity, rating or cost ordering |
| `minCost` / `maxCost` | 0 | Cost-for-two bounds |
| `expandCuisines` | false | Adds one listing per popular cuisine for the city |
| `expandCollections` | false | Adds the city's curated collections |
| `includeDetails` | true | Full detail page for each restaurant |
| `includeReviews` | false | Attach reviews or return review rows |
| `maxReviewsPerRestaurant` | 20 | 0 means all that Zomato exposes (guarded at 10,000) |
| `reviewSort` | Newest | Newest, oldest, highest or lowest |
| `includeMenu` | false | Attach dishes or return dish rows |
| `includeMenuImages` | true | Keep image-based menu page links |
| `includePhotos` | false | Attach photos or return photo rows |
| `maxPhotosPerRestaurant` | 30 | 0 means all that Zomato exposes (guarded at 5,000) |
| `maxItems` | 100 | Hard row cap for the run |
| `maxRetries` | 2 | Retries on 429, 5xx and connection errors |
| `ignoreUrlFailures` | true | Continue when one URL or restaurant cannot be read |

### Examples

Dining search, full details, top 50:

```json
{
  "mode": "search",
  "city": "bangalore",
  "searchMode": "dining",
  "minRating": "4",
  "maxItems": 50
}
```

Bulk discovery from a collection:

```json
{
  "mode": "collections",
  "startUrls": ["https://www.zomato.com/mumbai/insta-worthy"],
  "maxItems": 200
}
```

Every review and dish for one restaurant:

```json
{
  "mode": "menu",
  "startUrls": ["https://www.zomato.com/mumbai/pa-pa-ya-bandra-kurla-complex"],
  "maxItems": 500
}
```

```json
{
  "mode": "reviews",
  "startUrls": ["18619718"],
  "maxReviewsPerRestaurant": 0,
  "maxItems": 3000
}
```

## Coverage and honest limits

- **Live markets:** India and the UAE. The actor ships every city Zomato currently serves there, not a stale list. Cities Zomato left (London, New York, Singapore and others) are skipped.
- **Nine per listing:** Zomato's web listing returns nine restaurants per page. Bulk coverage comes from cuisine partitions, rating partitions and collections. Each collection can expose dozens of restaurants; `expandCollections` uses that.
- **Reviews:** paginated five at a time until the last page Zomato exposes. Very large restaurants can require hundreds of requests; `maxReviewsPerRestaurant` keeps runs predictable.
- **Menus:** text menus come from the delivery menu surface and include dish names, descriptions, prices, images and dietary tags. Some restaurants publish only menu photos; the actor then returns the image page links instead of inventing dishes.
- **Photos:** paginated 30 at a time across the all/food/ambience tabs.
- **UAE delivery:** Zomato does not publish delivery listings for UAE cities to signed-out visitors. Use Dining out, Cafes or Drinks & nightlife there; Delivery works for Indian cities.
- **Menus in the UAE:** many UAE dine-in venues publish no menu to signed-out visitors. When a restaurant has no text menu and no menu photos, Menu mode returns no row for it rather than inventing dishes.
- **Dates:** Zomato shows relative timestamps, so `reviewDate` is approximate and flagged as such. Exact dates are kept when published.
- **Blocking:** the actor picks its own connection path and retries automatically. A proxy input is deliberately not exposed.

## FAQ

**Do I need a Zomato login or cookies?**
No. Every mode works on public pages.

**Can I use IDs and links in the same run?**
Yes. `startUrls` accepts a mix of numeric IDs, share links, restaurant links and listing links.

**Can I scrape a city that is not in the dropdown?**
Yes. Paste that city's Zomato listing URL into `startUrls`, for example
`https://www.zomato.com/agartala/restaurants` or `https://www.zomato.com/sk/agartala/restaurants`.
The dropdown is a curated shortcut, not an exhaustive city index.

**Why do review links use `zoma.to`?**
That is the permalink Zomato publishes for a review. Some bot/HEAD checks reject the short-link
host even though it opens in a browser. If your tool needs a long URL, use
`https://www.zomato.com/<city>/<restaurant-slug>/reviews/<reviewId>`.

**Why does a search return fewer rows than `maxItems`?**
Because the selected listing or collection ran out of restaurants. Add cuisines, collections or more listings to widen the search.

**Why is one field missing from a row?**
Zomato did not publish it for that restaurant. Rows are omit-empty on purpose.

**Are menu prices final?**
They are the prices Zomato displays before taxes, delivery fees and charges.

**Does this actor write reviews or interact with restaurants?**
No. It only reads public data.

**Is this affiliated with Zomato?**
No. It reads public pages and is not endorsed by or connected to Zomato.

## Data source

Public Zomato web pages: city listings, collections, restaurant pages, delivery menus, review pages and photo galleries. The actor uses browser-like requests without login, keeps a polite request pace, and escalates its own connection path only when a block is real.
